In detail

This mainland residential municipalità (Chirignago, Zelarino, Gazzera, Cipressina, Trivignano) produced no evidence of a serious or ongoing crime wave in recent press coverage, and daytime life for residents and visitors appears unremarkable. The most substantive dated find is a Guardia di Finanza drug bust in Chirignago on 16 January 2026, where a man was arrested after police found over 700g of heroin, cocaine and hashish plus cash in what La Nuova Venezia described as a small drug-dealing operation — consistent with an earlier, larger 2021 Polizia Locale operation that dismantled a heroin-dealing point in the Zelarino countryside (900 doses seized). In 2026 Chirignago residents, mostly elderly, were also targeted by scammers posing as utility technicians to enter homes and steal valuables, part of a wider Mestre-area trend. VeneziaToday also reported a spate of car windows and windscreens smashed in a single raid in Cipressina. Notably, a March 2024 scare in Gazzera — a large police response to reported gunshots — turned out to be a false alarm with no victim or weapon found. No pattern of street robbery, assault, or organized violence specific to this district (as distinct from central Mestre or Venice's historic center) was found. Overall this reads as a quiet suburban area with only isolated, mostly non-violent, drug- and property-related incidents, warranting a cautious yellow at night rather than green given the documented drug operations. Sources checked: La Nuova Venezia (nuovavenezia.it); Comune di Venezia - Live (live.comune.venezia.it); VeneziaToday (veneziatoday.it); Il Gazzettino (ilgazzettino.it); Antenna Tre / Medianordest (antennatre.medianordest.it); Ultima Ora Live (ultimaoralive.it); Gente Veneta (genteveneta.it).
